hints.title: Composite Key Left Join
hints.text: Join Queries and npv table on both id and year columns.

hints.title: Missing Value Defaulting
hints.text: Queries with no matching entry in npv table must return an npv value of 0.

hints.title: Null Handling Function
hints.text: select q.id, q.year, ifnull(n.npv, 0) as npv from Queries q left join npv n on q.id = n.id and q.year = n.year.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT q.id, q.year, IFNULL(n.npv, 0) AS npv
FROM Queries q
LEFT JOIN NPV n ON q.id = n.id AND q.year = n.year;
```

complexity.notes: Composite hash join matches (id, year) in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner join omits queries that have no historical NPV record.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Left join preserves all query records with zero as default.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Multi-column left outer join paired with IFNULL or COALESCE.

solutions.approach: PostgreSQL Composite Left Join with COALESCE

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def npv_queries(npv: pd.DataFrame, queries: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = pd.merge(queries, npv, on=['id', 'year'], how='left')
    merged['npv'] = merged['npv'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return merged[['id', 'year', 'npv']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Multi-Column Left Merge and Fillna
